bug_semantics: DaoAuthenticationProvider equalizes username-existence timing by running PasswordEncoder against a dummy hash when UserDetailsService throws UsernameNotFoundException. AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate() still invokes DefaultPreAuthenticationChecks (UserDetails.isAccountNonLocked/isEnabled/isAccountNonExpired) before additionalAuthenticationChecks (the real passwordEncoder.matches). If a found user is locked, disabled, or account-expired, the pre-check throws and the expensive password comparison is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore distinguish those account attributes from both unknown usernames (dummy encode/match) and enabled accounts (real match) via response time (CWE-208).
flaw_origin: SEC-2056 commit c076f0f2e190c73a17379d05935c2c81657adee9 first wrote the dummy-password timing defense in DaoAuthenticationProvider.retrieveUser() while leaving the pre-existing preAuthenticationChecks-then-additionalAuthenticationChecks order unchanged. At the immediate parent, unknown usernames also skipped encoder work, so locked/disabled/expired users were not distinguishable from unknown users by password-encoder timing. That 2012 commit created the slow not-found path without a matching slow path for failed account-status checks.

Vulnerable 7.0.4 AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate() lines 157-158 and 168-169: preAuthenticationChecks.check(user) then additionalAuthenticationChecks(...). DefaultPreAuthenticationChecks (lines 331-353) throws LockedException/DisabledException/AccountExpiredException on !isAccountNonLocked/!isEnabled/!isAccountNonExpired before password matching.

Vulnerable 7.0.4 DaoAuthenticationProvider.retrieveUser() lines 102-115 / 146-157: prepareTimingAttackProtection() plus mitigateAgainstTimingAttack() dummy passwordEncoder.matches only on UsernameNotFoundException (SEC-2056 USER_NOT_FOUND_PASSWORD). Found-but-disabled users never hit that dummy match.

BIC git show c076f0f2e190c73a17379d05935c2c81657adee9: single-parent commit by Rob Winch, 2012-10-07, message SEC-2056 DaoAuthenticationProvider performs isPasswordValid when user not found. First wrote USER_NOT_FOUND_PASSWORD and retrieveUser() lines 103-105 dummy passwordEncoder.isPasswordValid(userNotFoundEncodedPassword, presentedPassword, null) before rethrowing UsernameNotFoundException.

Parent-tree verification: git show f3b143f677b80cddbdaac58c56a90d7bb1e4ac22:core/.../DaoAuthenticationProvider.java retrieveUser() catch UsernameNotFoundException only rethrows (lines 82-83); git grep USER_NOT_FOUND_PASSWORD on that parent is absent. Parent AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider already had preAuthenticationChecks.check(user) then additionalAuthenticationChecks (lines 148-149 / 156-157).

Later extract fd78d055aa5c2b1845445b78777882fe915e1845 (Phillip Webb, 2018, gh-4915) only lazily initialized/renamed the dummy-password helpers to prepareTimingAttackProtection/mitigateAgainstTimingAttack; it did not add the account-status skip and is a refactor, not the BIC.

git log -L 156,159 on 7.0.4 AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider shows the pre-check-then-password-check pair predates SEC-2056 (SEC-536 5e204e23f3975dcb7d1f727af177a3527b7f4132 and SEC-1187 6b53703e376a181c80689ce592ec68ad7d79f991); those commits are not this CWE-208 because encoder work was then skipped for unknown users as well.

reasoning: The advisory is a real CWE-208 in DaoAuthenticationProvider: the SEC-2056 dummy-password defense makes unknown usernames pay PasswordEncoder cost, but DefaultPreAuthenticationChecks still abort authenticate() before additionalAuthenticationChecks when isEnabled/isAccountNonExpired/isAccountNonLocked fail, so disabled/expired/locked accounts are observably faster. CVE.org/NVD status is Analyzed (not rejected) and GHSA withdrawn_at is null, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The smallest commit that first assembled that timing oracle is SEC-2056 c076f0f2e190c73a17379d05935c2c81657adee9, which wrote the dummy isPasswordValid path in retrieveUser(). Direct parent f3b143f677b80cddbdaac58c56a90d7bb1e4ac22 lacks USER_NOT_FOUND_PASSWORD and throws immediately on UsernameNotFoundException, so encoder timing did not yet separate unknown users from locked/disabled/expired users; the pre-check-before-password order already existed (SEC-536/SEC-1187) but is not itself this vulnerability. fd78d055aa only extracted/lazily initialized the dummy-password helpers and is a refactor, not a BIC. The 2012 object is a single-parent human commit by Rob Winch with no AI trailers, so AI is judged only on that BIC as NOT_AI. The direct fix is a317a3d8663995daa2bc91593bb88ae2da21ea52, which always runs additionalAuthenticationChecks even after a failed pre-check; it is in OSS tags 6.5.10 and 7.0.5 and absent from 6.5.9 and 7.0.4, matching the vendor patched boundary.
